I have posted bits and pieces of this before but I thought I would tie it all up in one neat package. You see before I retired I worked for an IBM business partner. As result I got a lot of old IBM Junk. One piece of Junk was an old Xserver 346 with the ServRaid 7 hardware RAID adapter but no disk drives or memory. Those Ultra320 SCSI drives used to cost an arm and leg. Well time marches on an I ran across a bunch of Ultra320 10K RPM 300GB SCSI drives for about $30 a shot. I ordered 6 of them for the X346 as well as a couple of sticks of memory. (The memory was more expensive than the drives)

This is where the trouble started. First you need a special CD to boot the ServRAID configuration program before you can even load anything. The ServRAID card has 256 Meg memory and a cache battery. This allows data that has not been written to disk and flushed from the memory to be retrieved in the event of a power failure. Well it just so happened that I had the latest and greatest ServRAID Support CD for the ServRAID 7. I booted the system (had a small problem with one of the Dual power supplies but that was fixed with a Re-seat of the power Supply. The X346 has hot swap-able power supplies. I flashed the firmware to the latest level and configured a 6 300 GB drive RAID 5 array. This gave me 1.4 TB of fast Disk.

The next problem was to load an operating system (THIS IS WHERE UBUNTU COMES IN). Since this was a junk box and the other half (the female half of the partnership called marriage) was already making comments about the cost of this project I had to go with the free is a very good price option. I originally wanted to go with Solaris but upon install it couldn't find the disk to load the operating system on. I decided to go with the Linux option. Well the same thing happened. All the linux distros couldn't find a disk to load a operating system on. At my wits end and down to the about to give the whole thing up, (and listen to Mommy Bear gripe about spending money) i tried Ubuntu Server 15.10. Ubuntu loaded like a champ. I set up a 200 GB partition on the on the ARRAY for a load and application partition and left the remaining 1.2 TB to be partition later.

Now I had my server and what to do with it. Well like a bolt out of the blue the problem arose. My wife does Genology and the four footed pointy ear ones who seem to think they are expert computer operators corrupted her data base. She had a back up copy of her data base on my desktop but is was about a month or so out of date. She had to move the data base back to her machine and then spend two months recreating the updates to the data base.

This is where I got creative. I bought a Zotac Zbox off ebay. I set this little dandy up as a wake up machine. It's only function is to wake up the rest of the computers in the house at 2:30 am. I have turned on the wake on LAN feature on all the systems. When the X346 wakes up it auto loads a back up program then connects to the other machines. It does a check of the client file systems that are to be backed up and if the creation time of the client file is the same as what is already in the back log the file is skipped and the next file is selected. If the creation time is different the file is backed up and the back up log is updated with the date and time of the backed up file.

When the backup of all the systems is complete the X346 Server powers down the clients and when all the clients are powered down it power it's self off.

One other addition to the system was the addition of a external LTO-3 tape drive. This allows me to back up the sever ARRAY on tape once a month or so. The Tape is then put into the safety deposit box at the bank.

So this is the sequence of events that demonstrated that with JUNK you can Always find a NEED.
